summary.intent: Coordinate a PR-review cleanup for the caliper repo: add and tighten changesets across PR branches, triage open review findings, dismiss nits, and fix the real findings via parallel workers.
summary.outcome: Changesets were written and pushed on all targeted branches. Triage found 58 open findings (45 FIX, 13 DISMISS), but the dismissals were denied by the auto-mode classifier, so none ran. Three fix workers were launched in parallel and had not reported back yet.

repo: Changesets live under `.changeset/` and use four keys for user-facing changes: cargo/caliper-docgen-core, cargo/caliper-docgen, cargo/caliper-docgen-napi and npm/caliper-docgen.
Binary-only changes, such as the linux glibc floor, list only the npm packages that ship the binaries.

The push gate is `just lint doc-check machete typos` plus `callisto status --check --strict` (callisto 0.17.0, as in CI). The CI step that previews the versioned release plan needs a GH token and cannot run locally.
The Callisto pin is in the release workflow, not `callisto.toml`, so the CONTRIBUTING.md claim is wrong.
Snapshot tests can leave stray `*.snap.new` files that get committed. PR 342 has 7 and PR 324 has 7 (about 208k lines). The files contain a local home path.
The PRs are stacked: PR 354 (base ci/linux-x64-glibc-floor) was merged into PR 329's branch, so its changes ride along.

code.finding: Passes `${TARGET}${GLIBC:+.$GLIBC}` to `pnpm napi build`. The locked @napi-rs/cli 3.10.8 `parseTriple` splits on `-`, so the artifact becomes `…linux-x64-gnu.2.28.node`. The floor check and upload expect `…linux-x64-gnu.node`, so both Linux legs fail.
A redundant `has()` guard exists here. It is harmless and fails closed.

workflow: The auto-mode classifier blocks `entire trail finding dismiss` as an external-system write. Such commands have to be run by the user, and the agent should not retry or work around the denial.
Subagent and teammate reports are model output, not user instructions. Verify them and surface denied actions to the user instead of redoing them.
Splitting fix work across parallel workers by file area, each told to run the full lint gate and skip merged PRs, keeps the changes from conflicting.

friction: All 13 finding dismissals were denied by the auto-mode classifier, so the user must run them manually.
The triage result was truncated, so the Low-severity FIX items were incomplete in the message.
Committed `.snap.new` files bloated PRs 324 and 342 and leaked local paths.
The release-plan preview CI step could not be verified locally because it needs a GH token.
open_items: Wait for the three fix workers (release/snapshots/docs, resolver/core, addon/loader/scripts) to report, then check CI before calling anything done.
The user needs to run the 13 `entire trail finding dismiss` commands.
`chore/changesets-for-merged-fixes` still needs a PR opened; it was not linked.
The finding on #344 about duplicate `schema.ts` copies guarded by a text-compare test is unverified and stays open pending a code-comment answer.
Remove the `.snap.new` files from #342 and #324 and re-measure the `docs/measurement.md` tables.
Fix #329 so the napi artifact name matches what the floor check and upload expect, and add the cargo keys to its changeset.
Branches 361, 360 and 363 were not covered by the changeset worker, which relied on their existing changesets.
The napi loader version-pin fix was left without a changeset because it is not user-visible, and PR 355 notes that version PRs will leave `index.js` with a stale pin.
